text: The episodic memory store keeps int8 quantized vectors in a sqlite-vec table.
Memory rows are written with their text and an embedding vector so recall can search by similarity.
sqlite-vec also provides an FTS5 keyword index that runs next to the vector table.
Hybrid search fuses dense similarity ranking with BM25 keyword ranking.
Reciprocal rank fusion adds one over k plus rank for each ranking source.
The fusion constant k defaults to sixty and each source has its own weight.
The semantic cache returns a stored answer when a new prompt is nearly identical to an earlier one.
Cache entries expire after a configurable number of days to avoid stale answers.
Empty answers are never cached because they would poison future lookups.
The token budget packs the system prompt, recalled memories and turns under a hard limit.
Think level low medium or high selects how many tokens a request may use.
When the prompt is too long the oldest turns are dropped before memories.
The circuit breaker opens a provider after repeated failures.
A half open breaker allows one probe call before closing again.
Fallback models take over while the primary provider breaker is open.
Checkpoints persist graph state so a swarm run can resume after a crash.
The checkpoint saver writes to SQLite in write ahead log mode.
Each conversation thread has its own thread id and checkpoint history.
OpenCL kernels compute batch cosine similarity on the Radeon GPU.
Without a GPU the same math falls back to NumPy on the CPU.
The GPU vector store does brute force top k search and not an approximate index.
API keys are stored in the macOS Keychain and never in YAML files.
The vault command sets and reads secrets by name.
Configuration files only hold environment variable names for credentials.
